records.title: The photoreceptor mosaic
records.design: Anatomical review of the human retinal photoreceptor mosaic
records.summary: Ahnelt describes how human rods and cones are distributed across the retina. Cone packing is especially dense near the fovea; different cone populations have different arrangements. This provides biological context for exploring local packing and sampling geometry in Vision Atlas.
records.finding: Ahnelt describes how human rods and cones are distributed across the retina. Cone packing is especially dense near the fovea; different cone populations have different arrangements. This provides biological context for exploring local packing and sampling geometry in Vision Atlas.
records.limitation: The review does not demonstrate a universal perfect hexagonal retina, tetrahedral visual processing, or a Fibonacci mechanism. It is anatomical evidence, not an EMDR treatment trial or a quantum-stability experiment.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Anatomical review of the human retinal photoreceptor mosaic. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

evidence.evidenceType: Anatomical review of the human retinal photoreceptor mosaic
evidence.measurement: Spatial sampling by retinal photoreceptor populations.
evidence.relationshipNote: Compare the Atlas geometry with measured local packing, density and irregularity; retain the differences between retinal regions.
evidence.reviewDepth: Publisher or author abstract and bibliographic metadata; selected explanatory sections where available.
evidence.hypothesisBoundary: Connections to M9 P24, Alpha, Beta, Gamma and Epsilon remain research hypotheses. Shared geometry does not establish a shared physical mechanism.

jadad.reason: Not a human randomised clinical trial.

records.title: Retinal origin of orientation maps in visual cortex
records.design: Computational model with comparative visual-cortex observations
records.summary: Paik and Ringach propose that interference between regularly spaced ON- and OFF-centre retinal ganglion-cell mosaics helps form orientation maps in visual cortex. Their model predicts hexagonal organisation of orientation-domain centres, with supporting patterns reported in four mammalian species.
records.finding: Paik and Ringach propose that interference between regularly spaced ON- and OFF-centre retinal ganglion-cell mosaics helps form orientation maps in visual cortex. Their model predicts hexagonal organisation of orientation-domain centres, with supporting patterns reported in four mammalian species.
records.limitation: This is a proposed developmental mechanism with supporting observations. It does not establish that all visual cortex follows this model, that humans prefer hexagons, or that retinal geometry stabilises quantum information.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Computational model with comparative visual-cortex observations. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

evidence.evidenceType: Computational model with comparative visual-cortex observations
evidence.measurement: Moiré interference between two spatial mosaics.
evidence.relationshipNote: Test whether similar interference mathematics generates useful candidate patterns in the Atlas, then evaluate each physical system separately.

records.title: Hexadirectional coding of visual space in human entorhinal cortex
records.authors: Matthias Nau; Tobias Navarro Schröder; Jacob L. S. Bellmund; Christian F. Doeller
records.design: Human fMRI during controlled visual tracking
records.summary: Nau and colleagues found a sixfold directional pattern in human entorhinal-cortex activity during a visual tracking task. The result supports a grid-like representation of visual space and gives Vision Atlas a measured example of sixfold organisation in brain activity.
records.finding: Nau and colleagues found a sixfold directional pattern in human entorhinal-cortex activity during a visual tracking task. The result supports a grid-like representation of visual space and gives Vision Atlas a measured example of sixfold organisation in brain activity.
records.limitation: An fMRI population signal is not a direct image of individual grid cells or proof of a tetrahedral eye mechanism. This study does not test Fibonacci sequences, EMDR outcomes, or quantum error correction.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Human fMRI during controlled visual tracking. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

evidence.evidenceType: Human fMRI during controlled visual tracking
evidence.measurement: Sixfold rotational modulation of a population-level neural signal with gaze direction.
evidence.relationshipNote: Use explicit rotational-symmetry tests with competing periodicities and independent data, rather than judging a pattern by visual resemblance.

records.title: Dynamically Generated Logical Qubits
records.summary: Hastings and Haah construct a honeycomb code in which a repeating schedule of two-qubit measurements creates logical qubits. Information protection comes from the code and measurement sequence acting together on the lattice.
records.finding: Hastings and Haah construct a honeycomb code in which a repeating schedule of two-qubit measurements creates logical qubits. Information protection comes from the code and measurement sequence acting together on the lattice.
records.limitation: The paper does not show that a passive hexagon alone protects information. Implementing this code requires the specified measurements and decoding; the current Aquila workflow does not implement that procedure.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Theoretical quantum error-correcting code. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

evidence.measurement: Dynamically generated logical qubits through scheduled two-qubit Pauli measurements.
evidence.relationshipNote: Use the measurement schedule as a separate theoretical benchmark; distinguish logical error correction from longer physical-qubit coherence.

records.title: The Penrose Tiling is a Quantum Error-Correcting Code
records.summary: Li and Boyle construct quantum error-correcting codes from Penrose tilings and variants based on Ammann–Beenker and Fibonacci tilings. Their construction connects nonperiodic geometric structure with the ability to recover information after local errors or erasures.
records.finding: Li and Boyle construct quantum error-correcting codes from Penrose tilings and variants based on Ammann–Beenker and Fibonacci tilings. Their construction connects nonperiodic geometric structure with the ability to recover information after local errors or erasures.
records.limitation: This is a mathematical construction in a preprint, not an experimental demonstration on Aquila. Its Fibonacci tilings are different from the Atlas M9 P24 sequences. A physical implementation and its resource requirements remain separate questions.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Theoretical preprint; version 2. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

evidence.measurement: Quantum information stored in a tiling-based code with local indistinguishability and recoverability.
evidence.relationshipNote: Study the explicit Fibonacci-tiling code and compare its mathematical requirements with our sequence representations before proposing a hardware mapping.

records.title: The IBM Quantum heavy hex lattice
records.authors: Paul Nation; Hanhee Paik; Andrew Cross; Zaira Nazario
records.summary: IBM explains why its heavy-hex architecture uses a sparse pattern of superconducting-qubit connections. The design reduces frequency collisions and unwanted effects on neighbouring qubits while balancing connectivity and the operations required by a calculation.
records.finding: IBM explains why its heavy-hex architecture uses a sparse pattern of superconducting-qubit connections. The design reduces frequency collisions and unwanted effects on neighbouring qubits while balancing connectivity and the operations required by a calculation.
records.limitation: This is a vendor technical explanation, not a peer-reviewed Fibonacci study. Its benefits depend on superconducting hardware and control choices; the shape alone is not evidence of universal quantum stability.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Hardware architecture explanation. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

evidence.measurement: Reduced connectivity to manage frequency collisions and spectator errors.
evidence.relationshipNote: Compare connectivity, noise and operation overhead explicitly when evaluating alternative geometries.

records.title: Surface code scaling on heavy-hex superconducting quantum processors
records.authors: Arian Vezvaee; Cesar Benito; Mario Morford-Oberst; Alejandro Bermudez; Daniel A. Lidar
records.summary: The authors combine surface-code layouts and pulse control on IBM heavy-hex processors. Increasing code size along one direction improves protection of particular logical states. Their analysis shows why both state directions and coherent noise matter when assessing error suppression.
records.finding: The authors combine surface-code layouts and pulse control on IBM heavy-hex processors. Increasing code size along one direction improves protection of particular logical states. Their analysis shows why both state directions and coherent noise matter when assessing error suppression.
records.limitation: Directional improvements do not establish general below-threshold scaling. The paper identifies further noise reduction needed for balanced scaling. It does not test Fibonacci or M9 P24 sequences.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Superconducting quantum-processor experiment and modelling. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

records.title: Enhancing detection of topological order by local error correction
records.authors: Iris Cong; Nishad Maskara; Minh C. Tran; Hannes Pichler; Giulia Semeghini; Susanne F. Yelin; Soonwon Choi; Mikhail D. Lukin
records.design: Numerical modelling and analysis of Rydberg-atom measurements
records.summary: Cong and colleagues use local error-correction ideas to identify topological order despite noise. They test the method numerically and apply it to measurements from a Rydberg-atom quantum spin liquid, making it directly relevant to analysing neutral-atom experiments.
records.finding: Cong and colleagues use local error-correction ideas to identify topological order despite noise. They test the method numerically and apply it to measurements from a Rydberg-atom quantum spin liquid, making it directly relevant to analysing neutral-atom experiments.
records.limitation: The method improves the diagnosis of a prepared state. It is not a demonstration that Aquila stores arbitrary information fault-tolerantly, and it does not test M9 P24 sequences.

records.title: Local stabilizer codes in three dimensions without string logical operators
records.summary: Haah constructs local stabilizer codes in three dimensions without string-like logical operators. The work introduces a different geometric organisation of information and errors, associated with the fractal structure of logical operations in the cubic-code family.
records.finding: Haah constructs local stabilizer codes in three dimensions without string-like logical operators. The work introduces a different geometric organisation of information and errors, associated with the fractal structure of logical operations in the cubic-code family.
records.limitation: This is code theory, not evidence that any fractal pattern stabilises a physical quantum computer. It does not demonstrate a Fibonacci connection or a complete self-correcting memory operating at finite temperature.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Theoretical three-dimensional stabilizer codes. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

evidence.measurement: Three-dimensional local constraints and non-string logical operators.
